title: New York vs London: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: New York for energy, 24/7 access, iconic American landmarks, and the best pizza on Earth. London for free world-class museums, pub culture, green spaces, and easy access to all of Europe via Eurostar.

categories.name: Daily Budget
categories.summary: NYC $200–350/day mid-range vs London £100–160/day (~$125–200). London is 25–35% cheaper overall.

categories.name: Food & Dining
categories.summary: NYC wins on pizza, bagels, delis, and 24-hour access. London wins on Indian food, modern British, and Borough Market.

categories.name: Museums
categories.summary: London's major museums are all free (British Museum, V&A, National Gallery, Tate Modern). NYC charges $28–30 per museum.

categories.name: Nightlife
categories.summary: NYC bars until 4am, 24/7 subway, legendary music and comedy venues. London closes earlier (pubs at 11pm).

categories.name: Green Space
categories.summary: London has more and larger parks spread across the city. Central Park is NYC's crown jewel but London has Hyde Park, Regent's Park, Richmond Park, and more.

categories.name: Day Trips
categories.summary: London: Paris in 2h15m by Eurostar, Oxford in 1h, Bath and Stonehenge. NYC: Philadelphia, Boston, DC — all good but no transatlantic options.

categories.name: Transit
categories.summary: NYC wins on 24/7 access. London wins on cleanliness, daily fare cap (~£8.10), and the Elizabeth line for Heathrow.

categories.name: Weather
categories.summary: London has milder, more consistent weather. NYC summers are brutally humid; NYC winters can be bone-cold.

categories.name: Iconic Sights
categories.summary: NYC: Statue of Liberty, Times Square, Brooklyn Bridge, Central Park. London: Big Ben, Tower of London, Buckingham Palace, Tower Bridge.

categories.name: Europe Access
categories.summary: London is a gateway to Europe — Paris, Amsterdam, Brussels within 2h by Eurostar. NYC requires a transatlantic flight to reach Europe.

faq.question: Is New York or London better for first-time visitors?
faq.answer: Both are legendary cities but they offer very different experiences. New York delivers maximum intensity. London is more manageable, free museums make it budget-friendlier, and the pub culture and green spaces give it a quality of life edge.

faq.question: Is New York more expensive than London?
faq.answer: New York is generally 20–30% more expensive. NYC mid-range hotels average $250–400/night vs London's £140–260/night. NYC tipping culture (20–25%) adds meaningfully to meal costs. London's free museums save $150+ over a week.
